title: Disconnect fallback and checkpointed output retention
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: During long-running streamed generations (chat or tool-invoking flows) client disconnects, transient timeouts, or slow external tools leave partially-produced outputs in memory or ephemeral caches. These partial generations can either be lost (leading to wasted work) or cause inconsistent application state if resumed incorrectly. Goal: Implement a client-aware checkpointing and cleanup protocol that: 1) periodically persists minimal generation state (checkpoints) enabling fast resume; 2) enforces a deterministic TTL and reclamation policy for orphaned partial outputs; 3) integrates with function/tool-calling so external invocation state is reversible or reattemptable on resume; 4) provides observability and metrics for partial-generation incidence and reclamation events.
acceptance_criteria: Periodic checkpoints emitted every 2s or every N tokens (configurable) for long-running streams
Each checkpoint is addressable by a short checkpoint_id returned to the client via stream frames and logged server-side
On client reconnect with checkpoint_id and same session token, server can resume generation from last checkpoint within 90th percentile latency of a fresh restart (target < 250ms overhead)
Orphaned partial outputs older than configured TTL (default 3h) are reclaimed and accounted in cost/usage telemetry
Tool/function call side effects invoked during partial generation are either completed atomically or rolled back/cancelled when resume is impossible; documentation covering limitations exists
End-to-end tests (unit + integration) covering disconnect during: a) noop-stream, b) tool call 1s, c) tool call 30s, and d) model-side timeouts
Console metrics surface: checkpoint-created, checkpoint-resume, checkpoint-expired, orphaned-output-reclaimed, resume-failures
implementation_notes: Checkpoint contents: minimal token index, KV-cache token pointer, last emitted structured-output frame metadata, active tool-call ids (opaque)
Storage: write checkpoints to ephemeral object store (ephemeral-s3) with lifecycle rule; metadata mirrored to primary DB for quick lookup
Checkpoint TTL default: 3h (configurable per-customer for Dedicated/Private); short-circuit reclaim path for low-latency nodes to avoid disk pressure

Resume flow: client sends resume request with session_id + checkpoint_id; server validates ownership and model-compatibility (model version, quantization profile); if incompatible, fallback behavior documented: either regenerate from scratch or attempt heuristic patching
Backpressure interaction: when backend queues grow, checkpoints will be forced more frequently (down to 1s) to minimize wasted compute when evictions occur

Tool calls: use an invocation manager that keeps idempotency keys and supports cancel/rollback or compensating actions. For third-party webhooks with no rollback, mark tool-call as 'completed-external' and require manual reconciliation on resume
Billing: partial-generation tokens associated with reclaimed checkpoints must be included in usage exports with a special reason code 'reclaimed_partial'
Security: checkpoint payloads contain no PII by default; customers can opt-in to include richer context in Private deployments; encryption-at-rest required
decisions: Persist checkpoints to ephemeral object store (cheap, lifecycle-managed) and mirror index to primary DB for fast lookup
Default TTL = 3 hours chosen to balance cost and rescue rate based on telemetry (empirical choose; future knob)
Expose checkpoint_id in stream control frames as short opaque token (10-12 chars) instead of full URIs
Resume requires session ownership; we will not support cross-account resume to avoid data leakage
For tool calls where rollback is impossible, prefer documentation and operator-visible flags over automatic destructive behavior
risks: Tool-call side effects incorrectly resumed leading to duplicated external effects; mitigation: require idempotency keys and conservative default of not re-invoking without explicit client opt-in
Increased storage/IO load from frequent checkpoints under heavy traffic; mitigation: adaptive checkpoint interval and on-node aggregation
Complexity in model-compatibility checks may lead to resume failures; mitigation: version pinning and clear retry UX
Potential cost disputes if reclaimed partial tokens are charged; mitigation: special usage codes and customer-visible logs
